changes: Kept the nun as the only person (donor), but the name is uncertain: Dayā, or possibly Sadyobhogā if dayā stands for dayayā ('out of compassion'). Explained in notes.
Removed 'pauna pānyāṃ' as residence (unclear; may be a locative place name or a corrupt word); recorded in notes.
Normalised the purpose wording; added a note that the find-spot is unknown and Bahilīṭola is the heading given by the edition.
Added a metrical note: an irregular śloka whose first quarter-verse has only 7 syllables.

place.as_written: Lalitpur (Patan), Bahilīṭola (on a stone reservoir at an unknown site in Patan)

purpose: gift of a stone water basin (śilādroṇī) by a nun for the welfare of beings (sattvānāṃ hitahetave)
notes: Fragment, badly damaged; R. 154. Undated. The verse is an irregular śloka: 'pauna pānyāṃ bhikṣuṇī | sadyobhoga dayā svayam | dattā eṣā(ṃ) śilādroṇī | sattvānāṃ hitahetave'. The first quarter-verse has only 7 syllables, so something may be lost. The donor is a bhikṣuṇī, but her name is uncertain: either 'Dayā', or 'dayā' = dayayā ('out of compassion') with the name hidden in 'sadyobhoga' (Sadyobhogā?). 'pauna pānyāṃ' may be a locative place name (the site of the gift) or a corrupt word, possibly part of a name. It is not used as a residence.
